title: Users and SSH
summary: Onboard a new baker: user, group, a shared folder that keeps its group, and key-based SSH from your laptop. Then fix a colleague's broken key login and deal with an account nobody remembers creating.

tasks.title: Welcome aboard
tasks.text: A new baker starts today. On **wafer**, create a group `bakers`, and a user `{{HIRE}}` with a home directory, `/bin/bash` as login shell, membership of `bakers`, and the temporary password `{{PASS}}`.

checks.fail_msg: There is no group bakers yet.
/home/{{HIRE}} is missing or not owned by {{HIRE}}.
{{HIRE}} is not in the bakers group.

checks.cmd: sshpass -p '{{PASS}}' ssh -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=4 {{HIRE}}@10.40.1.10 true
checks.fail_msg: Logging in as {{HIRE}} with the password {{PASS}} doesn't work.

hints: `useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G bakers {{HIRE}}`: `-m` creates the home directory, `-s` sets the shell, `-G` adds extra groups. (Debian's friendlier `adduser` asks questions interactively.)
`passwd {{HIRE}}` sets a password interactively; `echo '{{HIRE}}:{{PASS}}' | chpasswd` does it in one go.

steps.cmd: groupadd bakers && useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G bakers {{HIRE}} && echo '{{HIRE}}:{{PASS}}' | chpasswd

tasks.title: The shared recipe box
tasks.text: Create `/srv/recipes`, a folder every baker can work in and nobody else can even look into. Files created inside must automatically belong to group `bakers`, whoever creates them. (In octal, with that special bit: `2770`.)

checks.fail_msg: /srv/recipes is missing or its group is not bakers.
/srv/recipes should have mode 2770 (setgid + rwx for owner and group, nothing for others).
A file {{HIRE}} creates in /srv/recipes doesn't end up in group bakers.

hints: `mkdir /srv/recipes && chgrp bakers /srv/recipes` gives the folder to the group.

The **setgid** bit on a directory (the leading 2 in `2770`, or `chmod g+s`) makes new files inherit the directory's group instead of the creator's own group. `ls -ld` shows it as an `s` in the group's x position: `drwxrws---`.

tasks.title: Keys, not passwords
tasks.text: On **laptop**, create an SSH key pair and install the public key for `{{HIRE}}` on wafer, so that `ssh {{HIRE}}@wafer` logs in with the key, with no password prompt.

checks.fail_msg: Key-based login as {{HIRE}} from laptop doesn't work yet.

hints: On laptop: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519` (press Enter for the defaults). The private key `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` never leaves the laptop; the public one, `id_ed25519.pub`, is the one you hand out.
`ssh-copy-id {{HIRE}}@wafer` logs in once with the password and appends your public key to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the server, with the right permissions.

steps.cmd: test -f /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 || ssh-keygen -q -t ed25519 -N '' -f /root/.ssh/id_ed25519; sshpass -p '{{PASS}}' ssh-copy-id -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -i /root/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub {{HIRE}}@10.40.1.10

tasks.title: Marvin is locked out
tasks.text: Marvin, the head baker, says: *"My key worked for years. Then Gary 'fixed the permissions' and now it asks me for a password I never had."* His key is on laptop: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/marvin_key marvin@wafer`. The key is fine. Fix things on **wafer** so his key login works again.

checks.cmd: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=4 -i /root/.ssh/marvin_key marvin@10.40.1.10 true
checks.fail_msg: marvin's key login still doesn't work.

hints: sshd is picky on purpose (`StrictModes yes`): it ignores `authorized_keys` if the file, the `.ssh` folder or the **home directory** could be changed by someone other than the user. Anyone who could edit that file could add their own key.
Look at the whole path: `namei -l /home/marvin/.ssh/authorized_keys` shows every component's permissions.

The usual safe values: home `755` (or `750`), `~/.ssh` `700`, `authorized_keys` `600`, all owned by marvin. `chmod 755 /home/marvin && chmod 700 /home/marvin/.ssh && chmod 600 /home/marvin/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

tasks.title: Who is that?
tasks.text: While you're here: besides root, marvin and {{HIRE}}, **one more** account on wafer has a real login shell. Nobody remembers creating it. What is its user name?
hints: Every account is a line in `/etc/passwd`: `name:x:UID:GID:comment:home:shell`. Fields are separated by `:`.
System accounts have shells like `/usr/sbin/nologin`. `awk -F: '$7 ~ /bash|sh$/ {print $1, $3, $7}' /etc/passwd`, or `grep bash /etc/passwd`.

tasks.title: Shut the back door
tasks.text: Until someone explains `{{SNEAKY}}`, make sure it can't log in **at all**, not even with the SSH key that is sitting in its home directory. Don't delete the account: its files are evidence.

checks.fail_msg: The account or its home directory is gone. Restart the lab: keep the evidence!

checks.cmd: case "$(getent passwd {{SNEAKY}} | cut -d: -f7)" in /usr/sbin/nologin|/sbin/nologin|/bin/false|/usr/bin/false) exit 0 ;; esac; [ "$(passwd -S {{SNEAKY}} | awk '{print $2}')" = L ] && [ ! -s /home/{{SNEAKY}}/.ssh/authorized_keys ]
checks.fail_msg: {{SNEAKY}} can still log in. Hint: locking the password alone doesn't stop SSH keys.

hints: `usermod -L {{SNEAKY}}` locks the **password**. But SSH keys don't use the password, so that alone isn't enough.
Give it a shell that refuses logins: `usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin {{SNEAKY}}`. (Or lock the password **and** move its `authorized_keys` aside.)
Belt and braces: `usermod -L -s /usr/sbin/nologin {{SNEAKY}}`. `passwd -S {{SNEAKY}}` shows `L` when the password is locked.

solution.note: Next steps in a real incident: look at the account's files and shell history, `last {{SNEAKY}}` for logins, and find out who created it and when.
